# Synthetic Gambling AML Dataset — Data Dictionary

**This dataset is entirely synthetic**, generated by `generate_dataset.py`.
It is not derived from any real company's data, any take-home interview
assignment, or any real gambling platform's actual feature engineering.
The feature set was designed independently to represent the general shape
of an account-behaviour / anti-money-laundering detection problem, and is
safe for public portfolio use.

25,000 rows · ~1.5% positive rate (`is_suspicious_activity` = 1)

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `account_tenure_days` | Days since account creation |
| `customer_age` | Customer age in years |
| `kyc_verified` | Whether identity verification is complete (1/0) |
| `is_vip_tier` | Whether the account is in a VIP/high-value tier (1/0) |
| `num_deposit_methods_used` | Distinct deposit payment methods used, last 30 days |
| `num_withdrawal_methods_used` | Distinct withdrawal payment methods used, last 30 days |
| `deposit_count_30d` | Number of deposit transactions, last 30 days |
| `withdrawal_count_30d` | Number of withdrawal transactions, last 30 days |
| `total_deposit_amount_30d` | Total deposited, last 30 days |
| `total_withdrawal_amount_30d` | Total withdrawn, last 30 days |
| `avg_bet_size` | Average wager size |
| `num_devices_used_30d` | Distinct devices used to access the account, last 30 days |
| `num_distinct_ip_countries_30d` | Distinct countries seen in account IP addresses, last 30 days |
| `pct_deposits_near_reporting_threshold` | Fraction of deposits just under a reporting threshold (structuring indicator) |
| `median_hours_deposit_to_withdrawal` | Median time between a deposit and the next withdrawal (short = rapid cash-out / layering indicator) |
| `cross_border_payment_flag` | Whether cross-border payment methods were used (1/0) |
| `night_time_transaction_pct` | Fraction of transactions occurring at night (local time) |
| `is_suspicious_activity` | **Target.** 1 = flagged as suspicious, 0 = normal (~1.5% positive) |

## Generation approach

Each account's features are sampled independently from realistic
distributions (Poisson for counts, log-normal for monetary amounts, beta
for proportions). A latent "suspicion score" is then computed as a
weighted, noisy combination of known money-laundering risk indicators
(device/IP diversity, structuring, rapid cash-out, cross-border payments,
account age, KYC status), and the top ~1.5% by that score are labelled
positive — producing a dataset with genuine, non-trivial signal (ROC AUC
≈ 0.88 with a baseline classifier) rather than either pure noise or an
unrealistically easy separation.

## Regenerating

```bash
python generate_dataset.py
```

Deterministic (seeded), so re-running produces an identical dataset.
